description: We are a robotics team made up of Engineering Students in Electronics and Programming; we have participated in hackathons, university research projects and robotics skills at the university, national and international level and we like the idea of participating in this project already with intermediate knowledge in the areas of programming, electronics, aerospace.
summary:
NASA CIR-0G is an interactive 3D/2D microgravity combustion and fire-risk simulator built upon NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) datasets (BASS-II, FLEX, Saffire-I/III, and ACME). In microgravity, the absence of buoyancy creates spherical diffusion flames, cool flames, and toxic gas accumulation that behave fundamentally differently from terrestrial fires.

Our application allows astronauts, researchers, and students to test materials (PMMA Acrylic, Cotton Fabric, Propane Gas, n-Heptane) across 9 orbital and planetary regimes—including ISS, Lunar, Martian, and free-fall atmospheric reentry—while adjusting oxygen percentage, pressure (PSI), airflow, and igniter power in real time. A multi-threaded physics engine computes Damköhler extinction limits, burn rates, radiative heat flux, and toxic gas concentrations (CO2, HCN, HCl, NOx, SO2, HF), paired with an optional local AI safety analyst grounded strictly in NASA PSI records and historical spacecraft fire lessons (Apollo 1, Apollo 13, Mir).
details:
What it does & how it works:

NASA CIR-0G combines a real-time 3D/2D physics visualizer with a deterministic combustion engine and a local NASA knowledge base:

1. Real-Time Microgravity Physics (60 FPS): A dedicated Web Worker (with OffscreenCanvas 2D cross-section and WebGPU 256-particle compute / CPU fallback) solves spherical diffusion burn rates, Damköhler critical extinction (Da < 0.05), partial oxygen pressure limits (pO2 < 0.8 PSI), CO2 self-damping, Stefan-Boltzmann radiative loss, and toxic gas accumulation (SMAC limits). Moving any slider updates the flame geometry, temperature, and color spectrum live.

2. 3D Space & Chamber Visualization: Built with Three.js, featuring the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) quartz chamber, volumetric GLSL flame shaders, orbital environments (ISS, Moon, Mars, Earth LEO/GEO/MEO, Free-Fall Reentry with plasma friction shield), and smooth camera transitions.

3. Grounded Safety Analysis: Uses SQLite + ChromaDB vector search over NASA PSI benchmarks and official NASA combustion/safety documents. When the optional local LLM (via Ollama) is enabled, it receives the exact physics state to prevent hallucinations; users can also run in pure-physics autonomous mode ("zzz").

Benefits & Intended Impact:

- Provides an accessible, physically honest training and experimentation sandbox for spacecraft fire safety.

- Connects historical lessons (Apollo 1, Apollo 13, Mir 1997) and ISS PSI experiments with terrestrial firefighter spinoffs.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

- Backend: Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLite, ChromaDB, pandas, pdfplumber, httpx, Ollama (optional local LLM).

- Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES Modules), Three.js, WebGPU / OffscreenCanvas, Web Workers, GLSL shaders.

SI Disclosure (Code & Data):

AI coding assistants and optional local LLMs (Ollama) were used to accelerate software development, documentation, and optional in-app safety summaries, with deterministic physics equations and NASA PSI data enforcing factual accuracy.
